Yes. Several papers describe changing how many pages are fetched at inference time without retraining the retriever. ViSAR is the most direct match: it is a training-free adaptive-k retrieval method that dynamically decides the number of pages to retrieve from a query-conditioned page similarity matrix, reducing latency while maintaining or improving answer accuracy versus fixed top-k retrieval [1]. LAD-RAG also adaptively retrieves the necessary evidence based on the query and does so without top-k tuning, improving recall and QA accuracy with minimal latency [2].

Related methods vary in how they adapt retrieval. MAB-DQA dynamically reallocates retrieval budget across query aspects, and D2-ScaleAgent expands retrieval when more evidence is needed through an agentic routing loop [9,10]. LITTA controls the accuracy-efficiency trade-off by varying the number of query variants rather than directly choosing page count [6]. Q-REACT improves retrieval without retraining or rebuilding the retriever, but its abstract does not specifically say it dynamically changes the number of fetched pages [3].
